Two things encountered while capturing this batch of data

1. Assembling it ourselves vs. letting vLLM assemble it: identical results

Take the message set right before step 2 starts, on the same service, at the same moment, sent once down each of the two paths:

Pathprompt tokensOutput tokensreasoningcontent
Self-assembled harmony via /v1/completions1457136349 characters120 characters
Handed messages via /v1/chat/completions1457136349 characters120 characters

The first 120 characters of content are also identical, character for character. All four values match, which shows that the hand-assembled harmony string and what the server's openai_harmony renders are the same string — before, the only evidence was code-level "byte-for-byte comparison of the rendered result"; this time it came from an end-to-end run.

2. Same prompt, temperature 0, two runs come out different lengths

During collection, step 2 hit the max_tokens limit: 8192 output tokens, 401 message segments, with the model fabricating environment responses inside one single generation, writing turn after turn without ever emitting <|return|>. Resending the same prompt from the comparison table above (prompt tokens also 1457) once more finished normally with just 136 output tokens.

Steps 6 and 8 also hit the 8192 ceiling, in the same shape. This trajectory has 13 steps in total, 39088 output tokens altogether, of which three steps account for 24576.

These two numbers are only an observation. Why the same prompt at temperature 0 produces two different lengths, this page does not explain — no mechanism gets written until evidence is found.
